cards.meaning: greed; avarice — the excessive, harmful desire for wealth or power
cards.example: Ang kasakiman umano ng ilang opisyal ang naging ugat ng multi-bilyong pisong korapsyon sa flood control.
cards.exampleMeaning: The alleged greed of some officials was the root of the multi-billion peso flood control corruption.
cards.note: Noun form of the adjective 'sakim.' Carries a moral judgment — implies wanting more even when you already have enough, at others' expense; common in news framing the root cause of a graft case.

cards.meaning: agreement; pact — a formal mutual accord between two parties
cards.example: Bahagi ng kasunduan sa pagitan ng Pilipinas at India ang malawakang kooperasyon sa enerhiya at imprastraktura hanggang taong 2029.
cards.exampleMeaning: Part of the agreement between the Philippines and India is broad cooperation in energy and infrastructure through 2029.
cards.note: Refers to the accord itself, not the document — distinct from 'kontrata'/'kasulatan,' which name the paper. Preferred word for diplomatic accords since not every state-to-state understanding is a formal legal contract.
cards.tiesTo: Marcos BRICS summit / Philippines-India strategic partnership

cards.meaning: even; to the extent that — escalating adverb placed before the most extreme item in a list or argument
cards.example: 消费需求持续低迷，制造业利润甚至出现下滑。
cards.examplePinyin: Xiāofèi xūqiú chíxù dīmí, zhìzàoyè lìrùn shènzhì chūxiàn xiàhuá.
cards.exampleMeaning: Consumer demand continues to be sluggish; manufacturing profits have even declined.
cards.note: Mixed register — natural in both spoken analysis and formal writing. Signals the following clause tops everything said before it; distinct from 连…也/都… which requires bracketing the extreme item rather than standing alone.

cards.meaning: imported inflation — a fixed economic term for inflation driven by external costs (e.g. global commodity/energy prices) rather than domestic demand
cards.example: 输入性通胀掩盖了内需疲软的问题，情况甚至比数据表面显示的更严重。
cards.examplePinyin: Shūrùxìng tōngzhàng yǎngàile nèixū píruǎn de wèntí, qíngkuàng shènzhì bǐ shùjù biǎomiàn xiǎnshì de gèng yánzhòng.
cards.exampleMeaning: Imported inflation has masked the problem of weak domestic demand — the situation is even more serious than what the data shows on the surface.
cards.note: Contrasts with plain 通货膨胀 (inflation, cause-agnostic) — 输入性通胀 specifically diagnoses an external cost source rather than genuine demand strength; the exact diagnosis behind today's China data.
